manuscript_title: From pollination ecology to realized floral evolution in finite island populations
significance_statement: Pollinator-community change reaches floral evolution through several biological stages rather than one direct trait response. In one ecologically explicit plant–pollinator model, visitor functional matching determines finite pollen transfer and reproductive selection; the same outcrossing, selfing and Mendelian inheritance rules determine expected inherited change; and recruitment, survival, extinction and immigration determine which responses are realized in finite populations. Controlled visitor compositions can favour opposite floral-investment responses across plant starting states, whereas isolation-driven visitor assembly produces a coarse common deterministic direction. Reproductive assurance can preserve populations without prescribing one floral endpoint, and common final environments can retain different inherited states after different pollinator histories. Source-audited island systems contain the same ecological ingredients but lack the full inherited longitudinal transition. The model is ecologically explicit but not calibrated to natural rates, named flower traits or a particular archipelago.
ethics_statement: Not applicable to new data collection in this manuscript. The study reports simulations, a source-audited synthesis of published literature, and secondary analysis of published plant–pollinator data; it includes no new field sampling, specimen collection or experimental work requiring new approvals, licences or permissions.
data_availability: Primary numerical results derive from the frozen unified Model 3 reduction audit, the 19,968-case island campaign, deterministic genotype-density comparisons, finite-population ABM outputs, and source-locked real-island evidence reprojected by mechanistic layer. Historical Model 2 response-geometry, realized-richness, synthetic-k, response-rule, S/C/I and Gaussian/community-mean analyses are retained only as repository legacy provenance under legacy/model2/ and are excluded from the current Supporting Information and anonymous reviewer archive. The reviewer archive contains only the journal-facing manuscript, current Model 3 Supporting Information, current frozen Model 3 designs/results, source-readiness records needed for the active claim boundary, and current analysis scripts. Before final publication, accepted code and frozen analysis materials will be deposited in the Dryad Digital Repository with a persistent DOI.
